competitor_mentions.quote: We saw Dashlume advertising Slack-native alerts and wondered if Kataja has something similar, or a workaround via webhook?

narrative: Four tickets across five months, all minor and resolved within a week: a dashboard tile reset, an alert-routing question that name-checks a competitor in passing, a report export truncation, and an API pagination question. Tone is neutral and informational throughout with wide gaps between contacts and no repeat complaints on any issue. A textbook low-touch, healthy account.

This account generates frequent, varied faults across almost every module (dashboards, report builder, alerts, exports, API, connectors), with each individual ticket resolved in 1-2 days. But the recurrence rate is high — dashboard tile/blanking issues recur in October 2024 and again October 2025, alert faults recur in July and October 2025 — and a three-fault cluster on 2025-07-23/24 provoked 'please just get someone to look at the whole account' rather than another one-off fix request. Resolution speed hasn't dropped, but the customer's patience with recurring platform instability visibly has.

Low volume but two threads go quietly unresolved: an alert digest routed to the wrong distribution list, raised in December ('Not urgent over the holidays, but wanted it on record') and still unaddressed a month later ('Also still waiting on the alert distribution list issue from December'), plus a seat-usage report request that never gets a recorded answer. No anger anywhere, but this is the sparse, polite, meticulously logged pattern where nothing actually gets closed out.

Five tickets over four months end on two open issues: a connector setup wizard that errors at the credentials step with no fix recorded, and a dashboard that has 'gotten noticeably slower to load over the past couple of weeks, sometimes 15-20 seconds' with no resolution logged. Tone stays factual and unemotional throughout, but the most recent contacts are the least resolved, leaving the account exiting the window with an unaddressed performance regression.

A steadily worsening arc: a dashboard performance complaint notes 'I've raised performance issues before and they've been resolved, but this is now impacting daily work,' an API ticket asks the team to 'escalate if needed' after latency degraded from ~300ms to over 3 seconds, and by June the report builder is 'not functional... I need a response today' and stays unresolved. The next ticket names the pattern directly: 'Report builder was down for weeks and now this. At this point every month there's something new to chase.' Recurring faults that don't stay fixed, plus a core-module outage still open at period end, put this account at real risk.

Four tickets, all warm and low-stakes: a thank-you for a connector fix that let the team retire a manual Excel workaround, a routine setup question, and two feature ideas. No complaints, no repeat issues, engaged and satisfied throughout.

Very high ticket volume with faults clustering across nearly every module, often several in a single day ('Two issues in one day', 'Rough day', 'Third thing today'), sustained over a full year. Language is terse and clearly impatient but not escalating in severity over time — the export truncation issue explicitly recurs ('Second time in six weeks') suggesting the earlier fix didn't fully hold, but the customer keeps returning and reporting rather than pulling back, consistent with a high-friction but still-engaged relationship.

Frequent multi-module incident clusters through 2024 — five tickets in one day in February, five more in June, three in September, three in November — with 'enterprise account, need this prioritized' framing throughout. But the pattern tapers sharply into 2025: only a single minor ticket in February, opening 'Been quiet for a couple months.' The declining incident rate over time reads as a platform reliability problem that has genuinely settled down.

Sparse, low-stakes traffic over 18 months — plan guidance, a UI question, a sync-frequency question, a documentation nitpick — nearly all self-effacing in tone ('Might be user error, might be a bug'). One early seat-limit guidance request shows no recorded resolution, but nothing here reads as friction. Healthy, low-touch account.

Routine admin and minor-bug traffic spread over a year: bank connector swaps, a currency display bug, a decimal separator question. One dashboard filter-reset issue from November 2024 is never marked resolved and is never raised again, which may just mean it was dropped as unimportant. Overall tone stays even and undramatic.

competitor_mentions.quote: We looked at Storsund BI's alert digest layout during a recent vendor comparison exercise and it groups by severity, which is nice

narrative: Only three tickets over a year, all calm feature questions with no complaints and nothing left unresolved. The one item worth flagging to CS is that the account explicitly ran a 'vendor comparison exercise' that included a competitor, Storsund BI — a procurement-adjacent signal worth a check-in even though the request itself is mild and the relationship otherwise looks fine.

A clearly deteriorating account: alert configurations were wiped by a platform event for the second time ('it's really not good enough'), the report builder pivot view breaks and stays unresolved while the customer notes 'we've been raising issues fairly regularly this year and the response times have been frustrating,' and a subsequent total export outage takes 16 days to fix with the customer stating 'The state of reliability right now is genuinely unacceptable' and pointing back at the still-open report builder ticket. The next ticket, on connector data loss, cites eroded trust directly: 'our confidence in data integrity here is low.'
Two tickets, both routine and resolved without friction — a connector support question and a dashboard layout question. Nothing here signals concern.

Mostly routine traffic over a year (file size limits, billing contact update, credential expiry, a usage report request) resolved without drama. The account's most recent and only outstanding ticket is a functional one, though: the report builder freezes the browser on a 50k-row dataset, forcing the user to force-close and lose unsaved work, with no fix recorded.
A single minor permissions ticket, resolved in two days. Too little history to establish a trend, but nothing in what exists is concerning.

Sparse traffic but with a telling recurrence: a CRM connector duplicate-record issue from January is marked resolved, then explicitly comes back in May ('Same duplicate record issue as in January is back on the CRM connector'), with the customer now proposing 'a permanent fix rather than a manual cleanup each time' — accepting a workaround rather than expecting a real one. A report builder chart type the customer recalls using also appears to have vanished with no answer given. Low volume is masking a genuine, unaddressed reliability gap.

Warm, engaged account throughout: thanks for fast turnarounds, a feature request that gets built and is explicitly credited months later ('exactly what we asked for back in the spring'), and praise for the drill-down feature. Minor bugs are mentioned only in passing alongside positive feedback. This reads as a reference-customer profile, not a risk.

Steady mix of how-to questions and minor bugs (timezone default, an over-permissive sharing default, role clarification) resolved without incident. One connector setup ticket from September 2025 — a connection timeout with firewall rules checked on the customer's end — is the sole item left open, but nothing in tone suggests concern.

A long, chronic pattern of the same faults recurring despite each being logged as resolved: export truncation recurs at least four times over 18 months ('third time this year on the same board report' ... 'Export is truncating rows again. I know I've reported this exact thing before'), report builder save errors recur almost exactly a year apart ('same as last August'), a dashboard timeout recurs ('Fix from January didn't hold apparently'), and seat removal/billing is still broken at the final ticket despite multiple prior reports ('Billed for a seat we removed... actually fix the deletion this time'). The customer explicitly asks for root-cause fixes instead of repeat patches ('Can we get one root cause instead of four separate tickets?') — a sustained, visible loss of confidence in the platform.

A genuine recovery arc: months of compounding failures (connector re-auth, silent API sync failures, undelivered exports, a week-long new-hire access delay) culminate in an explicit escalation — 'I need this escalated to someone senior... Please have someone call me, not just reply to the ticket.' The customer later confirms real intervention followed ('Things have been calmer since your team called in June') and by September reports the API as 'rock solid... first stable week in months' and thanks the team for a report builder fix ('team's actually been able to focus on the reports themselves again'). One minor, explicitly non-urgent item (slower token refresh) remains open, but this is an escalation that worked.
